AgentCall.description:
One tool call the agent proposed (R135): the tool and its arguments as written, why code refused it
(empty when it ran), the result's note, the ids it returned, and how long it took.
AgentCall.title: AgentCall

AgentTrace.description:
How the agent answered (R135): every call, how many turns it took, why the loop stopped (the model
answered, or a cap was reached and it answered with the tools closed), the characters of every prompt
sent, and the citations code kept and dropped (ids no tool returned).
AgentTrace.title: AgentTrace

AnswerEvent.description: The answer with its trace and provenance, the question's wall-clock seconds and its cost.
AnswerEvent.title: AnswerEvent

CallEvent.description: A tool call settled: run (its result as JSON, cut at `RESULT_CHARS`) or refused (`call.refused`).
CallEvent.title: CallEvent

ChunkView.description: A passage as the provenance drawer shows it: its document, the heading context, and its text.
ChunkView.title: ChunkView

Citation.description: A chunk the answer relies on and the words it quotes from it.
Citation.title: Citation

CitationCheck.description:
One kept citation checked against its own content (R210), recorded, never enforced: which of the
answer's entities and whether its number that content holds, and for a chunk whether its quote is in
the whole passage (None: no quote, or no number given). R142's check reads every result offering a
cited id, notes and column names included; this one reads only what the id itself stands for.
CitationCheck.title: CitationCheck

ClaimHit.description:
A claim that claim retrieval found (R120): its observation, the chunk it was read from, its truth
fields as stored (truth is never left to the claim sentence's text, which an embedding and a full-text
analyzer both blur), and its siblings: the observations of the same canonical subject, predicate and
object whose triple has the opposite truth, with their chunks, so a disagreement is read together.
ClaimHit.title: ClaimHit

DatasetsView.description: The tabs, whether Neo4j answered, and the id of the dataset it holds (None: another graph, or none).
DatasetsView.title: DatasetsView

ErrorEvent.description: The question failed with an expected error (`KgBuilderError`); `message` says why.
ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent

ExactAttempt.description: One Cypher proposal of the exact route and what became of it.
ExactAttempt.title: ExactAttempt

ExactTrace.description: How the exact route answered, or why it gave up (then the question falls back to retrieval).
ExactTrace.title: ExactTrace

Fact.description:
One edge with its provenance: from a table (`source` names the file and rows) or from a text claim
(`evidence` is the sentence, `chunk_id` the passage holding it).
Fact.title: Fact

LLMEvent.description:
One LLM request: its model, whether the cache answered it, its tokens and latency, and its cost
(None when prices.yaml has no price for the model).
LLMEvent.title: LLMEvent

Link.description: The facts between two things of one type, drawn as one line.
Link.title: Link

LinkedNode.description: A graph node a question was linked to, and how.
LinkedNode.title: LinkedNode

ModelEvent.description: The model replied during `turn` after `ms` milliseconds.
ModelEvent.title: ModelEvent

PlanAttempt.description:
One plan the planner wrote: the plan as written, why it was refused (empty when it ran to the end),
the optional filters code dropped, and the steps it ran.
PlanAttempt.title: PlanAttempt

PlanStep.description: One step of a plan: an operation and the fields it uses (the others stay empty).

include_parts.description: find_claims: also claims about the records that are parts of the input.
include_parts.title: Include Parts

input.description: The index (from 0) of an earlier step whose result this step works on.
input.title: Input

label.description: find_entity: an optional node label or entity type; filter_records: the label to filter; related and rank: the label at the other end; about, and list and count of the records claims are about: only the records of this label.
label.title: Label

modality.description: find_claims: claims that hold (actual), may hold (possible) or hold under a condition (conditional).
modality.title: Modality

modality_words.description: The words of the question that ask for `modality`.
modality_words.title: Modality Words

name.description: find_entity: the name to look up, as the question writes it.
name.title: Name

object_like.description: find_claims: words for the claim's object.
object_like.title: Object Like

operator.description: How `property` is compared with `value`; rank by the value most records share: 'year' groups a date by its year.
operator.title: Operator

order.description: rank: most/fewest related items, highest/lowest property value, or with a property most/fewest: the value the most or fewest records share.
order.title: Order

property.description: filter_records: the property compared; related: a property of the relationship; list, sum, rank: the property read.
property.title: Property

relationship.description: related and rank: the relationship type followed.
relationship.title: Relationship

statement.description: read_check: the statement each candidate must support.
statement.title: Statement

subject_like.description: find_claims: words for the claim's subject.
subject_like.title: Subject Like

time_words.description: find_claims: words the claim's time must contain, quoted from the question.
time_words.title: Time Words

tone_words.description: The words of the question that ask for `tone`.
tone_words.title: Tone Words

truth.description: find_claims: claims the text states (affirmed) or denies (negated).
truth.title: Truth

truth_words.description: The words of the question that ask for `truth`.
truth_words.title: Truth Words

unit.description: count: count the items, their distinct documents, or the records claims are about.
unit.title: Unit

what.description: list: names of the items (name), or for claims the records they are about, their subjects or their objects.
what.title: What

PlanStep.title: PlanStep

PlanTrace.description: How a plan system answered (R74): its plans, and the fallback that answered when no plan could.
PlanTrace.title: PlanTrace

PropertyRow.description: A record's column value and the row it came from (the agent's `Property.source` format).
PropertyRow.title: PropertyRow

QueryPlan.description: An ordered list of steps; the last one, and only the last one, is a terminal.

steps.description: The steps, in order; the last ends the plan.
steps.title: Steps

QueryPlan.title: QueryPlan

QueryRecord.description:
One structured query the agent ran (R208), kept so the `q-` id an answer cites resolves within the
answers file: the tool, the statement and its parameters as run, what it read (record labels or tables)
and the source files behind them, and its result uncut (the agent saw the values cut at its cap). A
table row has no id of its own: the statement run again over the named staged file finds it.
QueryRecord.title: QueryRecord

RetrievalTrace.description: How the graph route chose its chunks, kept so a wrong answer can be traced to its cause.
RetrievalTrace.title: RetrievalTrace

Route.description: The route of the query stage that should answer a question (Step 2 scores its router on it).
Route.title: Route

SchemaView.description:
What the graph holds, by type: things per kind and type, facts per (source type, type, target type)
and origin, and the build's text size.
SchemaView.title: SchemaView

ScreenVerdict.description:
The security screen's decision on one request (R202, query/screen.py): allowed, or refused by `rule`
because of the words `matched`.
ScreenVerdict.title: ScreenVerdict

SentBackEvent.description: The reply of `turn` went back to the model once, for `reason`.
SentBackEvent.title: SentBackEvent

ShownChunk.description:
A chunk as the reader saw it: its id, the document it belongs to, and its text. R209: for a chunk the
agent cited after reading only a cut view of it (a `find_passages` excerpt, a `filter_passages` quote),
`text` is the whole stored passage and `excerpt` the view it read, so a quote is checked against the
source, not against one view of it (R182: three verbatim quotes failed against another view).
ShownChunk.title: ShownChunk

SourceRef.description:
An answer's source as the page knows it from the answer: its kind and id, and for a query the tables
it read, its columns, its rows and the record refs it listed (query/answers.py `QueryRecord`).
SourceRef.title: SourceRef

StepTrace.description: What one plan step did: how many items of each kind it produced, and a note (direction, checks).
StepTrace.title: StepTrace

Subgraph.description:
A drawable part of the graph: the things shown, the links among them, and how many things there are
in all (so the page can say what was left out).
Subgraph.title: Subgraph

SystemAnswer.description:
One system's answer to one question, with the chunks shown and its traces: the retrieval route's,
the exact route's (R71's graph system, and the text2cypher fallback of a plan system), the plans', the
agent's (R135), and the security screen's verdict when it refused the request (R202).
SystemAnswer.title: SystemAnswer

Thing.description:
A node as the interface draws it: its id (a record ref, a canonical id, or a mention id), kind,
type (a record's label, a text thing's entity type), display name and number of facts.
Thing.title: Thing

ThingDetail.description:
One thing with its properties, its facts (capped, `total_facts` in all), and the things at their
other ends.
ThingDetail.title: ThingDetail

WorksetMark.description:
The agent's verdict on one item of its working set (R211, variant `agent_workset`), as code checked
it: whether it included the item, the thing and quote it gave or why not, and whether the quote is
verbatim in the item (None: the item was not included).
WorksetMark.title: WorksetMark

post.description: Each source id -> the things it rests on (R223): what the page rings and focuses on the graph.

schema.title: Response Locate Api Datasets  Dataset Id  Locate Post
Response Search Api Datasets  Dataset Id  Search Get
